Asymmetric Domino Heck/Dearomatization Reaction of β‑Naphthols
to Construct Indole −Terpenoid Frameworks
Dong-Chao Wang, * Peng-Peng Cheng, Ting-Ting Yang, Pan-Pan Wu, Gui-Rong Qu,
and Hai-Ming Guo *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 7865 −7872 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A palladium-catalyzed enantioselective Heck cyclization/dearomatization cascade via capturing the cyclized Heck π-
allylpalladium intermediate by β-naphthols is reported, which provides a new strategy for the construction of chiral indole −terpenoid
frameworks. This method a ﬀords indole-functionalized β-naphthalenone compounds bearing an all-carbon-substituted quaternary
chiral center in excellent yields (up to 92%) and enantioselectivities (up to 94% ee). In addition, the utility of this method is
showcased by the gram-scale syntheses and diverse transformations of the dearomatized products.
I
ndole-terpenoids,1 such as indole monoterpenoids, indole
diterpenoids, and indolosesquiterpenoids, are a valued class
of natural products and exhibit a wide range of biological
activities, which often contain indole and hydrogenated
naphthalene sca ﬀolds. Mycoleptodiscin B ( I)
2 isolated from
the endophytic fungus Mycoleptodiscus sp. and penicilindole A
(II) isolated from the mangrove-derived fungus Eupenicillium
sp. display anticancer activity, whereas xiamycin A ( III)
isolated from Streptomyces sp. shows anti-HIV and HSV-1
activities ( Figure 1 ). Even some indole-ring modi ﬁed
analogues of natural terpenoids exhibit enhanced biological
activities relative to the parent natural terpenoid.
3 For example,
compared with totarol, indolototarol derivative ( IV, Figure 1 )
possesses better antimicrobial activity. 3a Therefore, discovering
an e ﬃcient route to synthesize indole −terpenoids and their
analogues is highly desirable.
The catalytic asymmetric dearomatization (CADA) reac-
tions of phenols have recently received great attention as a
powerful tool for constructing various chiral fused- or spiro-
ring systems from simple planar aromatic compounds.
4,5 The
corresponding CADA strategies, such as oxidation, alkylation,
arylation, amination, and halogenation, are also well devel-
oped.
4h Among them, transition-metal-catalyzed allylic alkyla-
tion reactions were ﬁrst employed in intramolecular asym-
metric dearomatization of phenol derivatives by Hamada 6a and
You.6b In 2013, You and co-workers demonstrated the ﬁrst

elegant intermolecular asymmetric allylic dearomatization
reaction of β-naphthols and allyl carbonates. 7a In 2017,
You7b and Zhong 7c developed the intermolecular asymmetric
allylic dearomatization reaction of β-naphthols and alcohols
(Scheme 1 a). However, all these allylic reagents initially
generate monosubstituted π-allyl intermediates and then form
allylic products containing 1,2-disubstituted alkene units. The
allylic precursors generating polysubstituted or ring-fused π-
allyl intermediates have not been utilized in the CADA
reaction of phenols, which would produce more diversi ﬁed and
complex allylic dearomatized products.
Since the late 1980s, as an e ﬀective pathway to construct
carbocyclic and heterocyclic frameworks, the domino Heck
reaction involving Heck cyclization/nucleophilic trapping of
the C −Pd intermediates has been extensively studied.
8,9
Concerning domino processes of N-(2-iodophenyl)-
allenamides via the capture of an indole-fused allylpalladium
intermediate, such as Heck/azide capture,
10 Heck/ketenimi-
nation,11 Heck/Suzuki,10b Heck/ﬂuorination,12 Heck/carbon-
ylation,13 and so on,14 have emerged as e ﬃcient approaches for
the construction of 3-substituted indoles. However, the indole
derivatives produced from the above sequences are often
planar molecules without a chiral center in the nucleophile
unit. In other words, the enantioselective construction of a new
chiral center by using a prochiral substrate to trap indole-fused
allylpalladium intermediate is a long-standing challenge.
During the course of our ongoing e ﬀorts on the CADA
reaction and domino Heck reaction, we envisaged that phenols
could be suitable prochiral nucleophiles for indole-fused
allylpalladium intermediates, and the domino process involving
the capture of such indole-fused allylpalladium intermediate
followed by the asymmetric dearomatization may provide a
new strategy for synthesizing chiral indole-terpenoid frame-
works. Herein, we report a new class of palladium-catalyzed
asymmetric domino Heck cyclization/dearomatization reac-
tion of β-naphthols with N-(2-iodophenyl)allenamides for
constructing indole −terpenoid analogues.
Initially, β-naphthol 1a and N-(2-iodophenyl)allenamide 2a
were employed as model substrates to optimize reaction
conditions. We ﬁrst tested a range of ligands in the presence of
Pd
2(dba)3 but did not obtain ideal results (see Table S1 ).
[Pd(C3H5)Cl]2 was subsequently used as the palladium source
to catalyze the model reaction. The combination of [Pd-
(C
3H5)Cl]2 (5 mol %) with commonly used ligands (10 mol
%), such as Trost L1, BINAP L2, and PHOX L3, in palladium-
catalyzed allylation reactions a ﬀorded poor results using
Cs2CO3 (1.5 equiv) as a base in toluene at 0 °C( Table 1 ,
entries 1−3). The desired reaction proceeded smoothly in the
presence of [Pd(C 3H5)Cl]2 and phosphoramidite ligand L4,
providing the desired product 3a in good yields, but with low
enantioselectivity ( Table 1 , entry 4, 80% yield and 30% ee,).
Employment of N-allyl phosphoramidite ligand allylphos L5
provided encouraging results giving the desired product 3aa in
81% yield and 88% ee ( Table 1 , entry 5). Inspired by You ’s

work,5g the ratio of [Pd(C 3H5)Cl]2 and allylphos L5 was then
examined. The result indicated that excess palladium ([Pd-
(C3H5)Cl]2/L5 = 1:1) a ﬀords higher enantioselectivity ( Table
1, entry 6, 88% yield and 92% ee). Next, we examined various
allylphos ligands L6−L12 in the catalytic system using excess
palladium ( Table 1 , entries 7 −13). However, the results were
no better than allylphos L5. Thus, allylphos L5 was selected as
the best ligand for the current domino Heck/dearomatization
reaction. Afterward, di ﬀerent solvents, bases, reaction concen-
trations, catalyst loading, and reaction temperatures were also
screened (Table 1, entries 14 −17; see also Tables S2 and S3 ).
The optimized reaction conditions obtained are as follows: 1
mol % of Pd(C 3H5)Cl]2, 1 mol % of L5, 1.5 equiv of Cs 2CO3,
1.0 equiv of 1a, and 1.2 equiv of 2a in PhCH3 (c = 0.1 M) at 0
°C under N 2 (Table 1 , entry 15). Notably, crystallization of
product 3aa from EtOAc/petroleum ether provided the
crystals of rac-3aa, and the enantiopurity of the product 3aa
in the mother liquid was improved to an excellent level ( Table
1, entry 18, 71% yield, >99% ee). Additionally, the absolute
conﬁguration of 3aa was determined to be the S-conﬁguration
by X-ray crystallographic analysis.
After the reaction conditions were optimized, a series of
allenamide substrates 2a−k with diﬀerent N-protecting groups
were examined. As shown in Table 2 , except for 2,4,6-
trimethylbenzenesulfonyl ( 3af, 67% yield, 69% ee), other
benzenesulfonyls with electron-donating groups slightly
aﬀected the yields and enantioselectivities ( 3aa−3ae,7 2 −
92% yields, 90 −93% ee). In contrast, Ns-protected allenamide
2g displayed good stereochemical control (83% ee), albeit with
a lower yield of 3ag (38%). N-Naphthalenesulfonyl allenamide
2h provided the product 3ah in good yield and enantiose-
lectivity (90% yield, 91% ee), whereas the use of acyl-protected
allenamides 2i−2k led to the corresponding dearomatized
products 3ai−3ak with moderate yields and ee values.
Furthermore, a series of β-naphthols and Ts-protected
allenamides were employed in the current domino Heck/

substituents in the benzene ring moiety of allenamides were
halogens ( 2l−2n, 2p−2r), the concerned reactions again
generated the corresponding dearomatized products e ﬀort-

To further explore the synthetic utility of this newly
developed methodology, the gram-scale syntheses of the
dearomatized products were carried out. As shown in Scheme
2, 2.5 mmol scale reactions gave the same results as the
optimized reaction conditions. Utilizing 1 mol % catalyst
loading, the domino Heck/dearomatization reaction of β-
naphthol 1a and N-(2-iodophenyl)allenamide 2a produced the
product 3aa in 90% yield and 93% ee, and the highly
enantioenriched 3aa (>99% ee) was obtained in 72% yield
after enrichment. The domino reaction of β-naphthol 1f and
N-(2-iodophenyl)allenamide 2a on a 2.5 mmol scale also
occurred smoothly to a ﬀord the product 3fa in 83% yield and
81% ee; the highly enantioenriched 3fa (96% ee) was obtained
in 56% yield after enrichment.
Diverse derivatization of the dearomatized products was
further demonstrated. As shown in Scheme 3 , the carbonyl
group of 3fa could be reduced with NaBH 4 to generate the
allylic alcohol 5 in excellent yield and diastereoselectivity.
Treatment of 3fa in THF at 0 °C with methylmagnesium
bromide and ((trimethylsilyl)methyl)lithium reagents a ﬀorded
the allylic tertiary alcohols 6 and 7, respectively, in excellent
yield and diastereoselectivity. Using catalytic hydrogenation
over the Pd/C catalyst, the α,β-unsaturated ketone sca ﬀold of
3fa could be reduced to a ﬀord the cyclohexanone 8 (52%
yield, 95% ee) and cyclohexanol 9 (39% yield, 95% ee, >20:1
dr) simultaneously. The cyclohexanol 9 was obtained in
quantitative yield without erosion of the enantiomeric purity
by treating cyclohexanone 8 with NaBH
4. In the presence of
magnesium and NH 4Cl in MeOH/C 6H6 (1:1), the cyclo-
hexanone 8 underwent a smooth detosylation to a ﬀord the
indole-terpenoid analogue 10 in 82% yield and 96% ee
(Scheme 4a). The hydroxyl group of cyclohexanol 9 could also
be oxidized to give cyclohexanone 8 in excellent yield and
enantioselectivity by treatment with PCC. Co(acac) 2/TBHP
caused benzylic oxidation of the cyclohexanol 9 to provide the
β-hydroxyl ketone 11, which then was transformed to α,β-
unsaturated ketone 12 (Scheme 4 b).
In addition, the linearity relationship between the ee value of
ligand L5 and product 3aa was determined. As shown in
Figure 2 , a clear linear correlation (coe ﬃcient of determi-
nation, R2 = 0.99) was observed in the catalytic reaction,
suggesting that a monomeric chiral catalyst might be involved
in the reaction ’s stereodetermining step.
In summary, we developed a palladium-catalyzed enantio-
selective domino Heck cyclization/dearomatization reaction of
β-naphthols with N-(2-iodophenyl)allenamides to synthesize
the skeleton of indole −terpenoids. This catalytic system
involves [Pd(allyl)Cl]
2 and a chiral phosphoramidite ligand,
facilitating the construction of indole rings and the
dearomatization of β-naphthols concomitantly. The optimized
reaction conditions aﬀorded a series of indole-functionalized β-
naphthalenone compounds with an all-carbon-substituted
quaternary chiral center in good yields (up to 92%) with
various enantioselectivities (up to 94% ee). Notably, the
protecting groups at the N-atom of allenamide and
substituents at the 3-position of β-naphthol had a great
inﬂuence on the enantioselectivity of the products. In addition,
the utility of this method was also showcased by the gram-scale
synthesis and derivatization of dearomatized products. More-
over, a linear relationship between the ee value of ligand L5
and product 3aa was observed.
